Match modules across species by ortholog overlap

Source: R/module_preservation.R
module_correspondence.Rd

Cross-tabulates the modules of two species over a paralog-resolved ortholog map. Tests each module pair for excess overlap.

Usage

module_correspondence(
  modules_ref,
  modules_test,
  map,
  species_ref = NULL,
  species_test = NULL,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

modules_ref, modules_test

Module assignments for the two species, from detect_modules() or as_modules().

map

Ortholog map from resolve_ortholog_map(), with gene1 in the reference species and gene2 in the test species.

species_ref, species_test

Optional species labels recorded on the result. module1 belongs to modules_ref, and that orientation cannot be recovered from the table, so supplying these lets classify_hub_conservation() catch a transposed call.

seed

Integer seed for the randomized-p draws behind pi0, or NULL (default) to draw from the ambient stream and leave it advanced. A seed draws from a private stream and restores the caller's on exit, the package-wide contract described under detect_modules().

Value

A list with pairs – a data frame of module1, module2, size1, size2, overlap, jaccard, p_value and q_value, one row per module pair – plus the species_ref / species_test labels. The column names match what classify_hub_conservation() expects.

Details

This answers "which module corresponds to which". That differs from whether a module's topology is preserved (module_preservation()). classify_hub_conservation() needs the correspondence, not the preservation call.

The map assigns one reference gene to each test-species gene, so the hypergeometric's independence assumption holds. The multi-copy expansion that made the same test anti-conservative under the retired gene-overlap engine is gone here: a HOG with three paralogs no longer contributes three correlated draws to the same urn.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
map <- resolve_ortholog_map(
  ortho, rownames(net_a$network),
  rownames(net_b$network)
)
corr <- module_correspondence(mods_a, mods_b, map)
subset(corr$pairs, q_value < 0.1)
} # }
